description: Uitdagingen-curation (Energietransitie): marker-enforcement op de afdeling-5.3-markers — de track is ruimtelijk blind (zone = AOI), precies dat is het verhaal. Derde scenario (SC-ET-NETCONGESTIE) is data-gegrond op de netbeheerder-capaciteitskaart.

scenarios.name: Art. 5.10 scope executed as spatial blockage
scenarios.description: FR-ET-01 (afdeling 5.3 scope over de hele AOI) is a conditional marker; enforcing it as exclusion would block the entire province — the toets has no spatial differentiation, and that is the policy point.

basis.provenanceNote: NC-ET-01 (art. 5.10) applies to new functions that can overload the grid, province-wide and without a GIO; this variant executes the strictest reading as a hard exclusion of the AOI.

scenarios.name: Art. 5.11 motivation duty dropped
scenarios.description: Drops FR-ET-03 (art. 5.11, energy paragraph with reporting duty) — an all-marker lesson: dropping a procedural marker changes no area at all.

basis.provenanceNote: NC-ET-03 (art. 5.11) requires an energy paragraph in the plan motivation; this variant documents that the duty is procedural by dropping it — expected delta zero.

scenarios.name: Netcongestie zones as spatial blockage (data-grounded)
scenarios.description: Excludes the transformer-capacity shortage zones published by the grid operators — a data-grounded hypothetical: no norm, but real data. Measures what data-driven congestion siting would cost versus the legally blind art. 5.10 marker.

basis.rationale: Art. 5.10/5.11 have no provincial zone layer (the marker is province-wide); grid-capacity zones are not a legal designation, so this scenario stays hypothetical — grounded in operator data instead of an arbitrary parameter.
basis.provenanceNote: NOT legally grounded: grounded in netbeheerder congestion data (see dataGrounding); the AOI-wide marker (NC-ET-01) is cited.
